title: Artifact transport and verification playbook for offline installs
content:
Purpose:
This is a focused playbook for moving verified runtime artifacts into customer air-gapped environments, and for the corresponding Terraform module decisions we need to capture. It consolidates transport formats, verification steps (checksums/signatures), offline registry layout, and a minimal upgrade path for patch/binary rollouts.

Scope and intent:
- Target audiences: solutions engineers, release engineers, and ops teammates preparing private installs for regulated customers.
- Not a full operator runbook (that exists in deploy-runbook.md). This doc is about the artifact lifecycle: build -> sign -> package -> transport -> verify -> register -> cleanup.

Key constraints we encounter often:
- No outbound internet from the target hosts.
- Strict change windows: upgrades limited to monthly maintenance windows.
- No persistent external credentials; ephemeral tokens allowed for import only.
- Customers with FIPS/KMS requirements (HSM-backed key use).

Bundle formats we will support (recommendation and tradeoffs):
1) OCI tar archive (skopeo save / crane) per image + index.json
   - Pros: standard OCI layout; containerd/CRI-compatible; can be loaded via ctr or crictl.
   - Cons: can be large; requires temp disk >= sum(image sizes) + working space.
2) Single compressed bundle (tar.gz) that contains:
   - registry-root/
   - helm-charts/ (package tgz)
   - operator-manifests/ (kustomize overlays)
   - runtime-binaries/ (systemd service bins, init)
   - third-party-deps/ (rpm/deb archives)
   - pros: single-file transfer, easier for USB / s3-offline transfer; cons: must verify internal manifest and checksums.
3) Delta upgrade patch bundles (rsync-friendly):
   - small set of layers/binaries; apply with a two-phase verify
   - recommended when bandwidth is low and upgrades are incremental.

Recommended artifact metadata (bundle-manifest.yaml fields):
- bundle_id: uuid
- version: semver
- created_by: CI-runner-id
- sbom_sha256: <sha256 of SBOM JSON>
- signature_cosign: <cosign base64 sig>
- images: [list of image refs + content-addressable digests]
- files: [path->sha256]
- install_order: [list of top-level steps e.g. load images -> install runtime -> apply manifests]

Signing and verification model:
- Primary recommendation: cosign signatures for OCI images and associated bundle-manifest.
- Secondary: detached GPG signatures for tar bundles where cosign can't be used.
- For high-security customers: support HSM-backed signing (PKCS11) and provide instructions to verify signatures against a customer-trusted certificate.
- Verification steps at customer site (minimal):
  1) Validate manifest sha256: echo '<sha>' > expected.sha && sha256sum -c expected.sha
  2) Verify cosign sig: cosign verify-blob --signature <sig> --key <public.pem> <bundle-manifest.yaml>
  3) Validate SBOM against known-good tooling (syft/tern).

Transport mechanisms (examples and commands):
- Preferred: encrypted S3 transfer into customer-controlled BOM bucket that their airgap proxy can access (prearranged). Use presigned URLs with very short TTL for inbound copy.
- Common: physical media (SSD/USB) using rsync over an authenticated scp or direct tar import.
- For registry import: use skopeo sync --src docker --dest dir to create an on-disk registry mirror, then rsync the registry-root to the target.
  Example: skopeo sync --spew --src docker --dest dir docker://registry.redwood.dev/redwood/model-server oci:/tmp/oci-mirror
- For direct OCI import to containerd: ctr images import /tmp/oci-mirror/*.tar
- For Helm charts: helm package . -> copy into helm-charts/ and index.yaml update via helm repo index --url <internal-url> .

Terraform module notes (architectural decisions):
- Provide two modules: bundle_registry (creates on-prem registry objects and ingress rules) and bundle_installer (handles local file unpacking and image load).
- bundle_registry variables: storage_backend (filesystem|minio), tls_cert_pem, registry_root, auth_mode (none|htpasswd|token), retention_policy
- bundle_installer variables: bundle_path, verify_signatures (bool), cosign_pubkey (optional path), install_service_account
- Important: modules must avoid requiring external providers during apply in the airgapped environment. Use local_file, null_resource, and the file provider instead of remote resource lookups. Document when a plan needs to be generated outside and the tfstate imported.
- Secrets handling: never put raw signing keys in TF. Use reference to KMS secret manager or documented manual step to import public keys post-apply.

Upgrade strategy (minor and patch upgrades):
Phase 0 - Pre-checks (by SE with customer): disk capacity, free inode count, package hash baseline, running pod health snapshot.
Phase 1 - Staged bundle import (off-hours): copy bundle, verify hashes and signatures, run dry-run installer that checks conflicts.
Phase 2 - Canary apply (if cluster allows): apply upgrades to a pinned subset (custom label) with automatic rollback hooks.
Phase 3 - Bulk rollout with rolling restart windows and health probes monitored.
Phase 4 - Post-upgrade validation: runtimes updated, SBOM delta matches expected, cost metrics sanity check.

Fallback and rollback options:
- Keep a copy of last-known-good bundle on the same host (readonly with immutable bit set).
- For container image rollback: docker/ctr pull fallback image from local registry path and reapply the old manifest.
- For helm releases: helm rollback <release> <revision> using local chart cache.

Operational notes and gotchas observed in the field:
- Some customers use aggressive endpoint proxies that rewrite TLS SNI. Recommend verifying certs at the kernel level (curl --resolve or openssl s_client) before large transfers.
- Busybox-based init images can fail to unpack some tar flags; prefer GNU tar for bundle creation and extraction.
- rsync over ssh with -W (whole-file) option is actually faster for very large single-file bundles on high-latency links.
- containerd version mismatches lead to 'unexpected EOF' on large layer loads; test image load on a dev host with exact distro/containerd version.

Operational checklist (pre-deployment):
- [ ] Confirm signed bundle received and manifest SHA matches recorded value in ticket
- [ ] Confirm cosign public key available and validated by customer
- [ ] Reserve maintenance window and notify stakeholders
- [ ] Backup etcd / cluster state before any change that touches control-plane images
- [ ] Verify disk space: required = sum(image sizes) * 1.5 + 10GB buffer

Minimal CLI snippets (copyable):
# Create OCI mirror of images
skopeo sync --src docker --dest oci docker://registry.redwood.dev/redwood/model-server oci:/tmp/oci-mirror
# Verify bundle manifest sha
sha256sum -c <(echo 'expected-sha  bundle-manifest.yaml') || exit 1
# Verify cosign signature
cosign verify-blob --key cosign.pub --signature bundle-manifest.sig bundle-manifest.yaml
# Import to containerd
ctr -n k8s.io images import /tmp/oci-mirror/*.tar

Notes for engineering follow-up (action items):
- Add a tf helper script that produces a terraform plan in the online CI, then serializes the plan and the expected state for offline import. (owner: Miguel)
- Add optional cosign attestation block into bundle-manifest generation (owner: Priya)
- Create test matrix: containerd versions, tar implementation, and rpm vs deb package installers (owner: Jonah)

Unresolved questions / open decisions:
- Do we want to standardize on OCI layout only, or keep tar bundles as first class? (tradeoff: customer ease vs internal simplicity)
- Formalize HSM-based signing and distribution flow for enterprise customers (process and legal acceptance).

Appendix (links and references):
- Internal CI job: github.com/redwood-inference/private-deployments/actions/workflows/bundle-pipeline.yml
- Cosign docs: https://github.com/sigstore/cosign
- Example sbom generation: syft packages --output json > sbom.json

Draft notes: this doc is intentionally informal; capture more customer-specific variants in separate playbooks (e.g., 'suse-only workflow', 'airgap-with-proxy').
